incumbent.name: Dave Faulkenberg
incumbent.summary: Dave Faulkenberg became Perry County sheriff in October 2025, chosen by a Perry County Democratic Party caucus to complete the term of retiring Sheriff Alan Malone {weht_faulkenberg}. He is not on the 2026 general-election ballot {in_list}.
record: 2015–2025: Alan Malone was chosen to fill the remainder of a sheriff's term in 2015 and elected to his first full term in 2018; in August 2025 he announced he would retire on or around October 1, citing the political climate and personal reasons {pcn_malone} {wfie_malone}.

Malone's tenure: the Perry County News credited him with partnering with the Tell City Police Department to start a National Night Out event and helping create a 16-week Citizens Police Academy {pcn_malone}.
October 2025: Faulkenberg was sworn in on Malone's last day, after the Perry County Democratic Party held a caucus in September to elect a sheriff to finish Malone's term {weht_faulkenberg}.

race_context: This is an open seat: appointed Sheriff Dave Faulkenberg is not on the ballot {weht_faulkenberg} {in_list}.
Both nominees were unopposed in the May 5, 2026 primaries: Democrat Bryce J. Hammack received 918 votes and Republican Roger Smith 563, in final results for all 11 voting locations {pc_primary}.
Coverage of the race is thin: no candidate questionnaires, forums or debates were found, and the Perry County News (published on the Dubois County Herald site) could not be reached during research.

candidates.summary: Bryce Hammack is a Tell City Police Department officer whose roles since 2004 have included detective, lieutenant and administrator, according to his campaign; he is the Democratic nominee {hammack_actblue} {pc_primary}.
background: His campaign says he has worked for the Tell City Police Department since 2004 as a reserve officer, patrol officer, K9 decoy, Indiana Law Enforcement Academy general instructor, firearms instructor, evidence officer, detective, lieutenant and administrator {hammack_actblue}.
Volunteer firefighter, Perry County Rescue member and Leadership Perry County graduate; studied criminology at Indiana State University, per his campaign {hammack_actblue}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, receiving 918 votes {pc_primary}; listed on the general-election ballot as a Democrat {in_list}.
on_incumbent: No statements about the current or former sheriff's record were found; his campaign page refers to campaigning for 'continued progress' {hammack_actblue}.
plans: No specific plans for the office were found; his campaign fundraising page does not list policy priorities {hammack_actblue}.
endorsements_finance: Accepts online contributions through an ActBlue page {hammack_actblue}; no totals, endorsements or campaign-finance reports were found.
gaps: Only his own campaign fundraising page was available; no news interviews, questionnaires or forum appearances were found.
No stated positions found on the jail, staffing and pay, budget, drugs, school safety or immigration enforcement.
